title: bhakti: the Narada Bhakti Sutras complete
hook: the last pages: what the people of this love are like, and the book's closing promise
carry: bhakti: the Narada Bhakti Sutras complete

segments.voice: Yesterday, bhakti as a taste that can't be told, like a taste for someone who cannot speak, a love that grows every moment. Did you let a love stay a taste? Day one thousand two hundred nineteen.

Two old friends meet after years apart and can't get a sentence out. One starts to speak and her voice catches. The other just laughs and wipes his eyes. Anyone watching knows exactly what's going on, though nobody has said a word. The last pages of the Narada Bhakti Sutras describe people like that, except the one they can't stop talking about is God. Today we finish the book: who these people are, how they live, and the promise it ends on.
screen: `OLD FRIENDS, NO WORDS.` → `VOICES CATCH.` → `THE LAST PAGES.`

segments.voice: The chief devotees, the sutras say, are those whose love has one direction only. When they talk with one another about the Lord, their throats choke, the hair on their arms stands up, and tears come. And they purify their families and the earth. Then a startling line: they make the holy places holy. They make actions good, and scriptures true. In this picture, people like these lend holiness even to the holy places. And then, among them, the sutras say, there is no distinction of birth, learning, looks, family, wealth or work. Why? Because they are his. Tadiyah. Belonging to him outranks everything else on the list. Then some practical advice. Don't lean on argument, the sutras say, because there's endless room for it and it settles nothing. Read the books of love instead, and do what wakes it up. Don't waste even half a moment. Keep up the plain virtues: not harming, truthfulness, purity, compassion, faith. Near the end the sutras say love, though one, takes eleven forms. Among them: love of his qualities and greatness, of his form, of worship, of remembering him. Love as a servant, as a friend, as a parent, as a beloved. Giving oneself entirely, being wholly absorbed, and the deep ache of separation. Then a list of teachers who agree, fearless of what people say, among them Vyasa, Shandilya, Garga, Hanuman and Vibhishana. And the last line, said twice at its close: whoever trusts and has faith in this teaching of Narada becomes a devotee, and reaches the most beloved. So the book that opened with now, then, we will explain bhakti, ends with a promise. Six days: love as the fruit, the king and the meal, the company of great souls, ripples and the crossing, a taste that can't be told, and today, the people of love. Tomorrow the Alvar hymns: Tamil poet-saints who sang their love for Vishnu aloud.
screen: `THROATS CHOKE, TEARS COME.` · `THEY MAKE HOLY PLACES HOLY.` · `NO DISTINCTION: THEY ARE HIS.` · `ONE LOVE, ELEVEN FORMS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: find your form. Sit, and let the breath settle. Let the sutras' forms of love drift past slowly. Love like a servant's, glad to help. Love like a friend's. Love like a parent's, watching over. Love like a beloved's. Love that remembers. Love that aches when apart. Don't choose. Just notice which one warms a little as it passes, toward God if you pray, or toward a person you love if not. Then stay with that one. The bell holds the time.
Bhakti. In the last pages of the sutras, one love in eleven forms, and its people, among whom there is no distinction, because they are his.
Your line: bhakti: the Narada Bhakti Sutras complete. Today, skip one argument you'd normally have, and do one small thing that wakes love up instead. Day one thousand two hundred nineteen.

howItsDone: In devotional Hindu communities, the closing sutras are read as a portrait of the ideal devotee, and the forms of love they list, such as servant, friend, parent and beloved, are familiar ways of relating to God in bhakti traditions.

fork.setup: you're among the devotees the sutras describe, and a sharp debater wants to argue about God all night. what do the sutras advise?
fork.reveal: vado navalambyah: argument isn't to be relied on, because there's endless room for it and it settles nothing. read the books of love, and do what wakes it up.

original.note: Sanskrit tadīyāḥ, 'they are his': the reason the sutras give for no distinctions among devotees.

trapdoor: what you thought: holy places make people holy.
what it means: the sutras say devotees make the holy places holy, and among them there are no distinctions, because they are his.
what a scholar hears: tīrthī-kurvanti tīrthāni; and the closing list of eleven āsaktis, from love of his greatness to the ache of separation, with ekadhāpy ekādaśadhā bhavati, one, yet elevenfold.

sources.ref: Narada Bhakti Sutras 67–73 (the single-minded devotees; tears and choked voices; they make holy places holy; no distinction among them, for they are his)
Narada Bhakti Sutras 74–79 (don't lean on argument; read the books of bhakti; don't waste half a moment; the virtues)
Narada Bhakti Sutras 82–84 (one love, eleven forms; the teachers who agree; the closing promise)

notes: Last day of the Narada Bhakti Sutras block (1214–1219): the teach names the block's days and points to the Alvar hymns.

'Eleven forms' is stated because sutra 82 says it directly (ekādaśadhā). The script lists the forms in sutra 82's order, grouped; confirm the renderings (guṇa-māhātmya, rūpa, pūjā, smaraṇa, dāsya, sakhya, vātsalya, kāntā, ātma-nivedana, tanmayatā, parama-viraha).
Sutra 83's list of teachers is shortened to five names (Vyasa, Shandilya, Garga, Hanuman, Vibhishana) with 'among them'. Confirm.
Sutra 72 (no distinction of jāti, vidyā, rūpa, kula, dhana, kriyā) rendered 'birth, learning, looks, family, wealth or work'. Confirm.
Sutra 63 (on what not to listen to) and sutras 56–66 generally are not covered in this block.

The 'Six days' look-back counts the block (1214–1219), not a claim about the text. The close's claim that the tradition holds the Alvar hymns as 'love like this, sung aloud' is a bridge line; confirm it is fair.

Editor pass: the holy-places line no longer overreads sutra 69 (devotees make holy places holier, not the source of their holiness); the bridge to the Alvars no longer claims what the tradition holds. The voice lists the eleven forms with 'among them' and makes no order claim; the earlier note's 'in sutra 82's order' should be checked, not relied on.
